notes.text: Zion's sake — Zion and Jerusalem are both put for the church, Heb. xii, 22. My peace - These seem to be the words of the prophet strongly resolving, notwithstanding all difficulties, to solicit God for the church's happiness, and constantly excite to the belief of it by his preaching, though it were long before it came, for Isaiah lived near two hundred years before this was accomplished. Righteousness - With reference to the Babylonians, understand it of the righteousness of God, who hath promised his people deliverance, and he must be righteous, and so understand salvation before; or rather, the vindicating of his people's cause in the eyes of the nations by the ruin of the Babylonians; he will shew that his people have a righteous cause. Lamp - And to that purpose is set up where it may be seen continually, to signify how eminently conspicuous this prosperous estate of the church should be among the nations, and as it may particularly relate to revealing of Christ unto the world.

A new name — The church shall be more renowned than ever, both in respect of her condition, and so called Hephzi-bah, and of her relation, and so called Beulah, and this new name the Lord gives them accordingly, ver. 4.

Crown of glory — An expression to set forth the dignity of her state. In the hand - Preserved and defended by God's hand. Royal diadem - The same thing with the former for substance. Or, the royal priesthood, whereof the apostle speaks, 1 Pet. ii, 9.

Forsaken — As a woman forsaken by her husband. Thy land - The inhabitants of the land. Hephzi-bah - My delight is in her; a new name agreeing with her new condition. Beulah - Married; agreeing to her new relation. Married - Thou shalt see the increase of thy children again in the land, as the fruit of thy married condition, which by reason of thy being forsaken of thy husband, were in a manner wasted and decayed: and this refers to the great enlargement of the church in the gospel days.

glossa.text:
*For Sion's sake.* ((HIER.)) The prophet in his own person, exceedingly gladdened by all those things which the incarnate Son confers upon the world. And this is it: *For Sion's sake I will not hold my peace,* however much he forbid him to speak, however much he threaten death.

*Let a lamp be kindled.* *Lampas* in Greek, *flamma* in Latin; whence: *I am come to cast fire upon the earth, and what will I but that it burn?* Set alight by this, the apostles spoke with divers tongues.
*A new name.* ((ID.)) It is the custom of the Hebrews to impose new names from new things, etc., *as far as* likewise first Simon, afterwards Peter.
*A crown of glory.* Of the faithful coming from all the parts of the world, as it were a crown.
*Thou shalt not be called.* He addresses the Church gathered out of either people, as if: thou shalt not be content with this end of appellations.
*And he shall rejoice,* etc. *For this cause shall a man leave father and mother ((Gen. II; Matth. XIX))*. *This is a great sacrament in Christ and in the Church ((Ephes. V))* .

notes.text: Thy mercy — Mine enemies are cruel and perfidious, but thou art infinite in mercy, and faithfulness. Heavens - Is infinite and incomprehensible. Faithfulness - The truth both of thy threatenings against thine enemies, and of thy promises made to good men. The clouds - Is far above our reach, greater and higher than we can apprehend.

Mountains — Stedfast and unmoveable: eminent and conspicuous to all men. Judgments - The executions of thy counsels. Deep - Unsearchable, as the ocean. Man - The worst of men; yea, the brute-beasts have experience of thy care and kindness.
Loving-kindness — Though all thine attributes be excellent, yet, above all, thy mercy is most excellent, or precious and amiable.

Satisfied — Who trust in thee, as he now said. Fatness - With those delightful provisions, which thou hast prepared for them in heaven. The river - Which denotes both their plenty, and their perpetuity.

Life — It is in God as in a fountain, and from him is derived to us. But - Of that glorious and blessed, and endless life, which alone is worthy of the name. Light - In the light of thy glorious presence, which shall be fully manifested, when we see thee face to face. Light - Joy and comfort, and happiness: the word light is elegantly repeated in another signification; in the former clause it is light discovering, in this light, discovered or enjoyed.

glossa.text:
*O Lord, in heaven.* ((Cass.)) Good things are from God through mercy. As if he should say: Evils are from man, but goods from mercy. O Lord, in those who are *heaven,* that is, who know hidden things, is thy mercy: and that they themselves are *clouds,* is from thee. ((AUG.)) Or *in heaven,* that is, mercy, etc., *as far as* but announces by sending forth his truth.

*Even to the clouds.* That is, the preachers, through whom God thunders in announcing, flashes in miracles, rains in teachings. Who are also mountains, whom the sun first clothes with light, which afterward, from them and yet not by them, descends to the lowest of the valleys: for they are ministers of teaching, but God enlightens.

*Thy judgments.* ((AUG.)) That thou hast mercy on these, and blindest those; they are utterly searchable to none: yet thou savest both, these bodily only, those spiritually as well, wherein is great mercy.
*Men,* etc. He shows that temporal things also are from God.

*They shall be inebriated.* ((ID.)) The thing cannot be expressed, but by this likeness he intimates that, being full, they lose their mind, so that they no longer recognize their own fathers, sons, and other friends. Or, then they are drunk in reality, who now hope. *With the torrent.* As if: There shall be a rush of grace and mercy to inebriate them. ((ID.)) *With the torrent.* Not that the beatitude should be passing, but plentiful. Or, thy will breaks all obstacles in man. Or, the wisdom of Christ is a torrent, because it is sudden and swift.

*For with thee is the fountain of life.* ((CAS.)) *With thee,* O Christ, *is the fountain,* that is, the beginning of every good; and *in thy light,* because through his preaching we see the light of the Father and of the Holy Spirit, and therefore *hold forth,* that in this world one may go more safely.

notes.text:
Now concerning spiritual gifts — The abundance of these in the churches of Greece strongly refuted the idle learning of the Greek philosophers. But the Corinthians did not use them wisely, which occasioned St. Paul's writing concerning them. He describes,

1. The unity of the body, ver. 1-xxvii,

2. The variety of members and offices, ver. 27-30,

3. The way of exercising gifts rightly, namely, by love, ver. 31, chap. xiii, 1. throughout: and adds,

4. A comparison of several gifts with each other, in the chap. xiv, 1. fourteenth chapter.

Ye were heathens — Therefore, whatever gifts ye have received, it is from the free grace of God. Carried away - By a blind credulity. After dumb idols - The blind to the dumb; idols of wood and stone, unable to speak themselves, and much more to open your mouths, as God has done. As ye were led - By the subtlety of your priests.

Therefore — Since the heathen idols cannot speak themselves, much less give spiritual gifts to others, these must necessarily be among Christians only. As no one speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed - That is, as none who does this, (which all the Jews and heathens did,) speaketh by the Spirit of God - Is actuated by that Spirit, so as to speak with tongues, heal diseases, or cast out devils. So no one can say, Jesus is the Lord - None can receive him as such; for, in the scripture language, to say, or to believe, implies an experimental assurance. But by the Holy Ghost - The sum is, None have the Holy Spirit but Christians: all Christians have this Spirit.

There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit — Divers streams, but all from one fountain. This verse speaks of the Holy Ghost, the next of Christ, the sixth of God the Father. The apostle treats of the Spirit, ver. 7, &c.; of Christ, ver. 12, &c.; of God, ver. 28, &c.
Administrations — Offices. But the same Lord appoints them all.
Operations — Effects produced. This word is of a larger extent than either of the former. But it is the same God who worketh all these effects in all the persons concerned.
The manifestation — The gift whereby the Spirit manifests itself. Is given to each - For the profit of the whole body.

The word of wisdom — A power of understanding and explaining the manifold wisdom of God in the grand scheme of gospel salvation. The word of knowledge - Perhaps an extraordinary ability to understand and explain the Old Testament types and prophecies.

Faith may here mean an extraordinary trust in God under the most difficult or dangerous circumstances. The gift of healing need not be wholly confined to the healing diseases with a word or a touch. It may exert itself also, though in a lower degree, where natural remedies are applied; and it may often be this, not superior skill, which makes some physicians more successful than others. And thus it may be with regard to other gifts likewise. As, after the golden shields were lost, the king of Judah put brazen in their place, so, after the pure gifts were lost, the power of God exerts itself in a more covert manner, under human studies and helps; and that the more plentifully, according as there is the more room given for it.

The working of other miracles. Prophecy — Foretelling things to come. The discerning - Whether men be of an upright spirit or no; whether they have natural or supernatural gifts for offices in the church; and whether they who profess to speak by inspiration speak from a divine, a natural, or a diabolical spirit.
As he willeth — The Greek word does not so much imply arbitrary pleasure, as a determination founded on wise counsel.

glossa.text: *Concerning spiritual things.* The Apostle begins to treat of the goods of the Holy Spirit, on account of whose greater gifts some grew proud, while the lesser envied and despised them, as though they would never have them.
*You know.* Being about to hand on spiritual things, he recalls the former things, that as they were then the image of idols, so now they may be the image of God.

*Therefore I give you to understand.* Because through the several graces they gave glory to men rather than to God, not knowing that this was ministered by the Holy Spirit; in all things he shows that the praise and the grace are God's, that as then the image of the idol was wholly an evil out of man, so now all good things may be believed to be from the Spirit of God. *No man in the Spirit,* etc. By thinking, by speaking, by working. *Saith* likewise in three ways, namely, by heart, by mouth and by work, anathema to Jesus, that is, some separation, from Jesus, that is, any sin whatsoever: as if: one is kept back through the Spirit from evil.

*But in the Holy Spirit.* As if: To work well, and every good, is through the Holy Spirit, and therefore let not the greater despise the lesser, because he has nothing save from the Holy Spirit.
*Divisions.* This is common to all: but the graces are divided, lest the lesser despair: lest the greater, while he hears of the graces, be proud.

*But the same God.* This he says, lest the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit should seem to work different things separately, from the fact that he had set graces under the Spirit, and ministrations under the Lord, and operations under God, referring all to the one God he adds: *Because God worketh. All in all.* He does not attribute all things to one, but works all things in all, so that what one has not in himself, he may have in another, and so charity and humility may abide.

*To every one.* The goods are divided, and are not given to the merit of anyone severally, but for the profit of building up the Church. We too have received the Holy Spirit, if we love the Church, if we are compacted together by charity, if we rejoice in the catholic name and faith. Let us believe, brethren, as much as each one loves the Church of Christ, so much has he the Holy Spirit.

*Of wisdom.* Wisdom is in the contemplation of eternal things. Knowledge, in the action of temporal things. Whence in Job: *Behold, piety.* That is, the worship, of God, *is wisdom,* which in Greek is *theosebia.* And what is this worship of him, save the love and the knowledge of him? But to abstain from evils is knowledge: and evils are in temporal things, in which one must be conversant warily and prudently. He to whom wisdom is given is as the sun; he to whom knowledge, a moon in the night of the world; they to whom the rest are given are stars: because these things are necessary in the night.
*To another, faith.* Faith too is among the gifts and endowments of God. Not therefore charity alone, but charity with faith is from God to us.
*Of speeches.* Speeches are the allegorical utterances which appear in the prophets and in the Gospels.

*One and the same spirit.* What he said above, that the three work, here he names the spirit: for because they are of one nature, what one works, the three work. One and the same, he says, lest there be thought to be as many as there are works: not that the Spirit works without the Father and the Son. For the operation of the Trinity is inseparable. *Dividing to every one.* Whence neither is this one to grieve, nor that one to be proud. *As he will.* Who alone knows what is fitting, and freely, not according to the merit of men.

notes.text: And the third day — After he had said this. In Cana of Galilee - There were two other towns of the same name, one in the tribe of Ephraim, the other in Caelosyria.

Jesus and his disciples were invited to the marriage — Christ does not take away human society, but sanctifies it. Water might have quenched thirst; yet our Lord allows wine; especially at a festival solemnity. Such was his facility in drawing his disciples at first, who were afterward to go through rougher ways.

And wine falling short — How many days the solemnity had lasted, and on which day our Lord came, or how many disciples might follow him, does not appear. His mother saith to him, They have not wine - Either she might mean, supply them by miracle; or, Go away, that others may go also, before the want appears.

Jesus saith to her, Woman — So our Lord speaks also, chap. xix, 26. It is probable this was the constant appellation which he used to her. He regarded his Father above all, not knowing even his mother after the flesh. What is it to me and thee? A mild reproof of her inordinate concern and untimely interposal. Mine hour is not yet come - The time of my working this miracle, or of my going away. May we not learn hence, if his mother was rebuked for attempting to direct him in the days of his flesh, how absurd it is to address her as if she had a right to command him, on the throne of his glory? Likewise how indecent it is for us to direct his supreme wisdom, as to the time or manner in which he shall appear for us in any of the exigencies of life!
His mother saith to the servants — Gathering from his answer he was about to do something extraordinary.
The purifying of the Jews — Who purified themselves by frequent washings particularly before eating.
The governor of the feast — The bridegroom generally procured some friend to order all things at the entertainment.
And saith — St. John barely relates the words he spoke, which does not imply his approving them. When they have well drunk - does not mean any more than toward the close of the entertainment.
And his disciples believed — More steadfastly.

glossa.text:
*And on the third day. ((AUG.))* After the showing forth of Christ through the testimonies of John, he himself shows himself by a miracle.

*And on the day.* It signifies that on the third day, that is, in the time of grace, after the time, that is, before the law and under the law, Christ came through the flesh to the nuptials of the Church.
*And there was called.* In which he shows that the nuptials which he made are not to be despised, and he intimates the sacrament of marriage.

*Failing.* The wine fails, that, wine being wonderfully made from water, the power of the hidden Godhead may appear.

((AUG.)) Greater is the power in the creation and governance of heaven and earth, etc., *as far as* through which the power that works also in the greater things is brought back to memory.
*What is it to me. ((ID.))* In these words he does not deny his mother, as the heretics say, etc., *as far as* he understands the entrance to God, he drinks the wine.

*Two or. ((ID.))* It belongs to one making an estimate to speak thus, so that he should call the same vessels two-measure which he also calls three-measure, etc., *as far as* sown abroad by the three sons of Noe.

*And they filled them.* That the waterpots were filled at his command signifies that that Scripture also is from the Lord; but while Christ lies hidden in it under the veil, that is, under the covering of the letter, it tastes of insipid water. But when the veil is taken away, it is wine that inebriates. He could indeed have filled them, empty as they were, with wine, he who creates all things out of nothing; but he chose rather to make wine out of water, that he might teach that he does not destroy the law but fulfil it, nor in the Gospel does he do or teach other things than those which prophecy foretold.

*And when he had tasted.* The *triclinium*, that is, three ranks of those reclining, standing apart from one another in height: that is, teachers, the continent, the married. The chief steward is some man skilled in the law, who drinks the spiritual sense of the law. Whence to open the spiritual sense in the Scriptures to disciples is to turn water into wine, as when after the resurrection he opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures. *The water made wine.* By the water, the baptism of John; by the wine, the passion of Christ: whence the wine also is carried first to the chief steward, that is, to John, who drank the passion before Christ did.

*This he did. ((HIER.))* In the beginning of the signs which, being mortal, he was to give to mortals, he turned water into wine; and as, being now immortal, he opened the understanding of the disciples, that in the law and the prophets they might understand Christ, so he first steeped carnal minds with the savour of wisdom, being about afterwards to fill them, when raised again, with a greater glory.

echoes.text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they don’t speak. They have eyes, but they don’t see. They have ears, but they don’t hear. They have noses, but they don’t smell. They have hands, but they don’t feel. They have feet, but they don’t walk, neither do they speak through their throat.
echoes.note: Paul recalls the Corinthians being led to 'mute idols' (eidola aphona), echoing the psalm's taunt that the nations' idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands, with mouths that cannot speak. The motif of the idol's speechlessness contrasted with the living God is a fixed OT polemic, and the verbal link (mouths/speech) gives this strong volume.

echoes.text: “What value does the engraved image have, that its maker has engraved it; the molten image, even the teacher of lies, that he who fashions its form trusts in it, to make mute idols? Woe to him who says to the wood, ‘Awake!’ or to the mute stone, ‘Arise!’ Shall this teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in its midst.
echoes.note: The dumb idol that cannot teach, the woe to one who says to a mute stone 'Awake,' undergirds Paul's phrase 'mute idols.' Habakkuk stresses that there is no breath/spirit in the idol, which sharpens Paul's contrast with the speaking, Spirit-empowered confession 'Jesus is Lord' that follows.

echoes.text: They bear it on the shoulder, they carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands, from its place it shall not move: yes, one may cry to it, yet it can not answer, nor save him out of his trouble.
echoes.note: Isaiah mocks the idol that is carried, set in place, and cannot move or answer when cried to; it does not save. Paul's image of being 'led away to mute idols, however you might be led' coheres with this picture of a powerless, voiceless god, reinforcing the speech/no-speech antithesis.

echoes.text: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they can’t speak. They have eyes, but they can’t see. They have ears, but they can’t hear; neither is there any breath in their mouths.
echoes.note: A close parallel to Psalm 115, again ridiculing idols with mouths that do not speak and no breath in their mouths. Its recurrence in the same idol-polemic tradition raises the volume of the 'mute idols' echo, though the verbal contact is generic.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
echoes.note: Paul's claim that only by the Holy Spirit can one confess 'Jesus is Lord' anticipates the chapter's pneumatology, faintly resting on the promise that God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh so that they prophesy. The connection is thematic (Spirit-enabled speech) rather than verbal here.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
echoes.note: The 'varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit' poured out on the community reflects the eschatological outpouring of one Spirit producing diverse manifestations (sons, daughters, old, young prophesying and dreaming). The one-Spirit/many-recipients structure coheres tightly with Joel's vision, which Paul elsewhere cites for the Spirit's universal distribution.

echoes.text: Yahweh came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more. But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested on them; and they were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran, and told […]
echoes.note: God takes of the one Spirit on Moses and distributes it among the seventy elders, who then prophesy; Moses wishes all the Lord's people were prophets. This is the paradigmatic OT scene of one Spirit apportioned to many for varied ministry, mapping onto Paul's 'same Spirit... various kinds of service.'

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: The Spirit of the Lord resting as a sevenfold endowment (wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, fear) on the messianic shoot offers a precedent for one Spirit yielding plural gifts. The catalog form is suggestive, though Paul's list differs in content.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: Paul's enumeration of Spirit-gifts beginning with 'word of wisdom' and 'word of knowledge' echoes the messianic Spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel, and knowledge. Both passages catalog distinct charisms flowing from a single divine Spirit, giving coherence to the allusion even where the lists do not match item-for-item.

echoes.text: Yahweh came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more. But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested on them; and they were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran, and told […]
echoes.note: The Spirit distributed by God among many recipients, each prophesying, anticipates Paul's 'distributing to each one separately as he desires.' The sovereign apportioning of one Spirit to diverse people for prophecy and service is the structural backbone shared with the Mosaic narrative.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
echoes.note: Prophecy as the signature gift of the poured-out Spirit ('your sons and daughters shall prophesy') stands behind Paul's list, which prominently includes prophecy. The eschatological democratization of the Spirit coheres with Paul's 'to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit.'

echoes.text: He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding; he reveals the deep and secret things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him. I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.
echoes.note: Daniel praises God who gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding, and reveals deep and hidden things. The pairing of God-given 'wisdom' and 'knowledge' as revelatory gifts faintly parallels Paul's first two charisms, though no verbal citation is made.

echoes.text: and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all kinds of workmanship,
echoes.note: God fills Bezalel with the Spirit of God in wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and all craftsmanship for the tabernacle. This is the OT prototype of the Spirit equipping individuals with specific skill-gifts for the building of God's dwelling, resonating with Paul's Spirit-distributed abilities for the body's upbuilding.

echoes.text: For she that is the architect of all things taught me, even wisdom. For there is in her a spirit quick of understanding, holy, Alone in kind, manifold, Subtil, freely moving, Clear in utterance, unpolluted, Distinct, unharmed, Loving what is good, keen, unhindered, Beneficent, loving toward man, Stedfast, sure, free from care, All-powerful, all-surveying, And penetrating through all spirits That are quick of understanding, pure, most subtle:
echoes.note: Wisdom describes the spirit of wisdom as manifold (poikilos), intelligent, all-powerful, pervading all spirits, distributing benefits. The notion of one Spirit with manifold operations apportioned among many coheres with Paul's 'various kinds of gifts... the one and the same Spirit works all,' making a Second-Temple sapiential backdrop plausible.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them, “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘These are the living things which you may eat among all the animals that are on the earth. Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat. “‘Nevertheless these you shall not eat of those that chew the cud, or of those who part the hoof: the camel, because he chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, he is […]
echoes.note: John explicitly notes the six stone jars were set 'after the Jews' way of purifying'; the Levitical purity code (clean/unclean, washings) is the institution being named. Volume is high (direct reference to the purification system) and Coherence is strong: Jesus transforms the water of ritual purification into the wine of the new age, signaling supersession of the old cleansing rites.

echoes.text: “Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the one treading grapes him who sows seed; and sweet wine will drip from the mountains, and flow from the hills. I will bring my people Israel back from captivity, and they will rebuild the ruined cities, and inhabit them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink wine from them. They shall also make gardens, and eat their fruit.
echoes.note: The eschatological promise that the mountains shall drip sweet wine and the hills flow with it stands behind Cana's superabundance (six jars of 20-30 gallons each become the best wine). Coherence is high: John frames the sign as the dawn of the messianic age in which the prophets' image of overflowing wine is realized. Availability and Recurrence of the wine-of-the-age topos across the prophets strengthen the echo.

echoes.text: It will happen in that day, that the mountains will drop down sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters, and a fountain will flow out from Yahweh’s house, and will water the valley of Shittim.
echoes.note: Joel's day-of-the-Lord vision of mountains dripping with new wine belongs to the same prophetic abundance-of-wine cluster that informs Cana. The figural logic is that Jesus' first sign inaugurates that promised day. Coherence with John's 'his hour' / eschatological framing supports the reading though the verbal contact is thematic not lexical.

echoes.text: In this mountain, Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of choice wines, of fat things full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.
echoes.note: Isaiah's eschatological banquet on Zion of rich food and well-aged wines for all peoples is the messianic-feast type that Cana's wedding banquet enacts. Volume is moderate (banquet + choice wine); Coherence is strong since the ruler praises the 'good wine kept until now,' echoing the aged-wine motif. The wedding setting reinforces the feast typology.

echoes.text: Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine; he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes. His eyes will be red with wine, his teeth white with milk.
echoes.note: Jacob's blessing of Judah, who 'washes his garments in wine' with eyes darker than wine, is a classic messianic-Davidic prophecy of wine-abundance attached to the coming ruler from Judah. Second-Temple readers (cf. Targums) read this messianically, so Availability is strong. Cana's prodigal wine figurally fulfills the Shiloh oracle's vinous excess.

echoes.text: You shall no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall your land any more be termed Desolate: but you shall be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for Yahweh delights in you, and your land shall be married. For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons shall marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
echoes.note: Isaiah names restored Zion 'married' (Beulah) and depicts God rejoicing over her as a bridegroom over a bride. The Cana wedding, where the bridegroom motif surfaces and Jesus implicitly assumes the true bridegroom's role, figurally enacts this nuptial covenant imagery. Coherence with John's bridegroom Christology strengthens the link.

echoes.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahweh.
echoes.note: Hosea's promise that the LORD will betroth Israel to himself forever in righteousness and faithfulness is foundational to the YHWH-as-bridegroom typology activated at a wedding where Jesus quietly occupies the bridegroom's place. Availability and Recurrence of the divine-marriage theme support a figural echo. Hosea 2:21-22 also pairs betrothal with abundance of grain, wine, and oil.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “This is the statute of the law which Yahweh has commanded. Tell the children of Israel to bring you a red heifer without spot, in which is no defect, and which was never yoked. You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring her outside of the camp, and one shall kill her before his face. Eleazar the priest shall take some of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle her blood toward the front of the […]
echoes.note: The water of purification / red-heifer lustration ordinance is part of the specific 'purifying' system John references with the stone jars (stone vessels in particular resisted impurity per Second-Temple halakhah). Coherence supports it: the water-for-cleansing motif is precisely what Jesus repurposes. Slightly lower volume than Leviticus since John's phrase is general.

echoes.text: They shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow to the goodness of Yahweh, to the grain, and to the new wine, and to the oil, and to the young of the flock and of the herd: and their soul shall be as a watered garden; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.
echoes.note: Jeremiah's restoration oracle promises radiance over the LORD's goodness, the grain, the wine, and the oil, with mourning turned to joy. The new-covenant abundance (same chapter as the new covenant) coheres with John's inaugural sign of joy and wine. The contact is thematic and the echo faint.

echoes.text: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved. Beloved
echoes.note: The Song's wedding/erotic imagery of wine ('your love is better than wine,' the bridegroom and bride) supplies a nuptial-wine matrix that John's wedding sign may evoke, especially given the bridegroom motif. Volume is diffuse and the echo is faint and contested, but Coherence with John's broader bridegroom Christology (cf. 3:29) supports listing it.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, “In this you shall know that I am Yahweh. Behold, I will strike with the rod that is in my hand on the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood. The fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river.”’” Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their […]
echoes.note: The first Mosaic sign turned water into blood; John's first sign turns water into wine, a possible deliberate Moses/Jesus typological inversion (curse vs. joy). Coherence with John's broader Moses Christology (1:17) gives it some weight, but the contrast is subtle and the echo contested.

echoes.text: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works.
echoes.note: The sapiential exhortation to drink wine with a merry heart as God's gift frames wine as a sign of divine favor and joy, the affective register of Cana's abundance. Volume is low and the link diffuse; listed as a faint wisdom-tradition resonance.

echoes.text: Wine is as good as life to men, If you drink it in its measure: What life is there to a man that is without wine? And it has been created to make men glad. Wine drunk in season and to satisfy Is joy of heart, and gladness of soul:
echoes.note: Ben Sira's praise of wine as gladness of heart 'created from the beginning for joy,' drunk in season, supplies a deuterocanonical wisdom backdrop to Cana's celebratory wine. Availability is solid (Second-Temple sapiential text); the echo is thematic and faint.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: John 2:1 'on the third day' may complete John's opening week (day-counting from 1:29, 35, 43) evoking the seven-day creation framework that the Prologue's 'In the beginning' inaugurates, making Cana a new-creation climax. The echo is structural and contested but coherent with John's deliberate Genesis 1 architecture.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
echoes.note: 'On the third day' as a marker of restoration/raising ('on the third day he will raise us up that we may live before him') may color John's 'third day' at Cana, anticipating resurrection-glory language that returns at 2:19-22. Coherence with the chapter's later three-days-temple saying supports a faint thematic echo.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Your steadfast love, O Lord, extends to the heavens.
With you is the fountain of life.
The water blushed into wine, and the best was kept for last.
With you is the fountain of life.
He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: A wedding running out of wine, an ordinary feast on the edge of embarrassment.
In you is the fountain of life.
Six stone jars, plain water, a quiet word — and abundance no one ordered.
In you is the fountain of life.
This is the sign of the kingdom: the best is not behind us; the best is still being poured.
In you is the fountain of life.
So bring your empty jars, your run-dry places; the glory of God is generous.
In you is the fountain of life; we drink and are glad!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A feast run dry; plain water poured.
In you is the fountain of life.
Six stone jars, a quiet word, abundance.
In you is the fountain of life.
The best is still being poured; bring your empty jars.
In you is the fountain of life. Amen.
